one_line: Temporary 123 cannot bid as prime because the latest Q&A confirms a 100% certified SDVOSB set-aside, and the flooring work falls outside its documented capabilities.
scope: The VA seeks flooring demolition, preparation, replacement, installation, and related services at Baltimore VAMC, the entire Loch Raven campus, and Perry Point VAMC in Maryland. This is a flooring BPA RFQ, despite the Special Notice label, with a revised base period of December 1, 2026–November 30, 2027, plus four option years.
fit: Maryland falls within Temporary 123's stated nationwide work area.
The company has federal facility-support experience, but none of the supplied past performance establishes flooring installation or healthcare infection-control experience.
Office trailers and sanitation facilities could support incidental contractor needs, but the notice does not establish a separate trailer-rental procurement.
red_flags: Hard eligibility barrier: November 10 Q&A confirms certified SDVOSB eligibility; Temporary 123 has SBE and MBE status and no stated SDVOSB certification.
Mandatory walkthroughs occurred October 20–21, 2026. The latest Q&A requires a bidder member to have attended; Temporary 123's attendance is undocumented.
NAICS 238330 and PSC N055 are absent from the company profile. Its listed GSA SINs—532490P, 561210FS, 561210FAC, and 541614—do not establish flooring coverage.
The documented fleet and price list cover temporary facilities, not flooring installation crews, materials, or rates.
Same-date November 10 documents conflict on quantities, CLIN numbering, and VA-furnished versus contractor-furnished materials; their precedence is not established.
The LPTA versus best-value conflict is not clearly resolved by the full Q&A; the response to question 15 refers to order limits.
No minimum task-order size or guaranteed volume; fixed annual pricing must absorb stated material, freight, tariff, and product-discontinuation risks, with no substitutions.
Insurance limits remain unclear, bonding is unanswered, and specific license requirements are not established in the supplied procurement text.
competition: The HigherGov AI summary identifies Fidelity Contract Flooring as a possible related incumbent under BPA 36C24523A0027, reported at $3,033,053; this is not confirmed as the incumbent for all current sites. Supplied records show repeated Fidelity flooring awards, commonly with one offer. Carpet Resources received a $21,214 Perry Point flooring award with 22 offers, and G3 Venture Hub's Baltimore record lists 17 offers. Current offers received are not supplied.
price_signal: Reported related Fidelity BPA value: $3,033,053. Other supplied Fidelity flooring awards include $1,396,970, $1,441,234, and $149,691; the Perry Point award was $21,214. These differ in scope and duration and do not establish unit rates. Current Q&A sets a $6,000,000 BPA ceiling and $1,500,000 order limit, neither guaranteed. Temporary 123's trailer prices provide no usable flooring benchmark.
must_have: Certified SDVOSB prime eligibility. Source: November 10 Q&A, set-aside responses.
A bidder member must have attended the October 20–21 walkthroughs covering Baltimore, Loch Raven, and Perry Point. Sources: Amendment #3 and November 10 final Q&A.
Best and final quote covering all three sites and flooring requirements, due November 18, 2026, at 2 p.m. Eastern Time. Source: Amendment #3.
Quote the base year and all four option years; total five-year price is evaluated. Sources: November 10 Q&A, evaluation response and question 72.
Meet the 50% services limitation on subcontracting, measured by base/option period under 852.219-73(e). Source: November 10 Q&A, subcontracting response.
Provide an onsite designer/project manager with at least COR Level 1 certification for each project, plus project-specific safety/QC personnel. Source: November 10 Q&A, questions 27–29.
Perform required ICRA/PCRA controls and furnish barrier materials; comply with OSHA and manufacturer warranties. Source: November 10 Q&A, questions 24, 29–30, and 63.
Use specified Tarkett materials without substitutions and cover stated pricing risks in annual fixed rates. Source: November 10 Q&A, questions 53 and 72–73.
Comply with Baltimore WD 2015-4265, Revision 35, and Cecil County WD 2015-4215, Revision 33, including applicable wages and benefits. Sources: November 10 wage attachments.
Maintain applicable insurance; the asbestos provision applies even when separate Government personnel perform abatement. Source: November 10 Q&A, questions 74–80.
